rows.name: McDonald's Corp.
rows.statement: The Committee has resolved to assign a BUY recommendation for McDonald's Corporation with a conviction score of 0.909. The dominant argument carrying the majority was that McDonald's 95%-franchised model constitutes a durable royalty and rent collection mechanism generating high-quality recurring income, and that the current valuation — trading below its five-year median EV/EBITDA multiple — offers a favorable entry point for a business of this caliber. Three of four members ultimately endorsed this position, with Mr. Greenblatt upgrading from PASS after acknowledging that negative book equity from share buybacks had obscured the true return-on-capital profile. The most significant dissent came from Ms. Wood, who maintained a PASS at low conviction, arguing that McDonald's lacks platform convergence and disruptive growth potential relevant to her forward-looking mandate. This dissent did not prevail because the Committee judged the investment on risk-adjusted return and franchise durability rather than speculative innovation criteria. The Committee recommends initiating a position at current levels.

rows.name: Nike Inc.
rows.statement: The Committee has resolved to issue a BUY recommendation on Nike, Inc. at the current price of $37.30. The dominant argument, carrying a clear majority across three of four members, holds that Nike's durable consumer franchise — evidenced by 38% global market share, 22% mental market share, proven pricing power, and decades of superior returns on capital — is materially mispriced at current levels, with sentiment near cyclical lows and the "Pace" restructuring offering a credible catalyst for margin recovery. The most significant dissent, advanced by Ms. Wood, argued that Nike is a legacy defender of an existing market rather than a platform for disruptive innovation, warranting a PASS. This view did not prevail because the Committee judged it applied an innovation-platform framework misaligned with the valuation question before us: not whether Nike will disrupt, but whether its enduring competitive advantages are adequately reflected in today's price. The Committee concludes they are not, and recommends initiating a position at current levels.

rows.name: UnitedHealth Group Inc.
rows.statement: The Committee assigns UnitedHealth Group a BUY with a conviction score of 0.875. The dominant argument, endorsed unanimously by Messrs. Buffett, Marks, and Greenblatt, is that UnitedHealth represents a high-quality compounder—anchored by durable switching costs, vertical integration across insurance, PBM, care delivery, and analytics, and earnings power growing at 13–16% annually—available at approximately 16.6× forward earnings, a meaningful discount to intrinsic value. The most significant dissent came from Ms. Wood, who issued a PASS on grounds that convergent platform disruption (AI-driven care, autonomous delivery, genomic cost deflation) could structurally erode the incumbent model. This view did not prevail because the Committee judged it a category error: the relevant question is not whether disruption risk exists but whether it is adequately compensated at current prices, and the consensus held that it is—substantially so. The Committee recommends initiating a BUY position in UNH at prevailing levels, with periodic reassessment of regulatory and technological developments.

rows.name: Amazon.com Inc.
rows.statement: The Committee adopts a BUY position on AMZN with a conviction score of 0.724. The dominant argument carrying the majority held that AWS represents early-innings AI infrastructure buildout rather than a mature business, with 37% revenue growth, 35%+ operating margins, and a $25 billion-plus annualized AI run rate growing at triple digits — positioning Amazon's $220 billion capital expenditure program as a durable competitive moat rather than a liability. The most significant dissent, advanced by members Buffett and Greenblatt, argued that current valuation offers insufficient margin of safety given the magnitude of capital deployment required and the difficulty of calculating reliable return-on-capital and earnings-yield metrics across Amazon's blended segments. This dissent did not prevail because the majority judged that applying mature-business valuation frameworks systematically undervalues platform-scale infrastructure assets during a regime shift in AI adoption. The Committee recommends initiating a BUY position in AMZN at current levels, with capital expenditure return trajectories as the primary monitoring variable.

rows.name: Alphabet Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns Alphabet Inc. a BUY rating with a composite score of 0.714. The dominant argument carrying the majority, advanced most forcefully by Leopold Aschenbrenner and supported by Howard Marks and Cathie Wood, holds that Alphabet is undergoing a regime-shift transition in which AI becomes its primary growth vector — with 82% Cloud growth, custom TPU infrastructure, the Gemini model family, and 950-million-MAU consumer distribution creating a full-stack advantage that traditional valuation frameworks systematically undervalue. The most significant dissent came from Warren Buffett and Joel Greenblatt, who argued that an EV/FCF multiple of approximately 71x conflates a wonderful company with a wonderful investment and that current pricing already capitalizes the AI upside. This dissent did not prevail because the majority judged the valuation reset from peak enthusiasm, combined with the scale and velocity of AI-driven revenue inflection, to offer asymmetric upside that static earnings-yield analysis fails to capture. The Committee recommends initiating a BUY position at current levels.

rows.name: American Express Co.
rows.statement:
## Furton Research Investment Committee — Official Statement

**American Express Co. (AXP) | Final Position: BUY | Score: 0.684**

After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns American Express a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.684. The dominant argument, advanced by the majority and led by Messrs. Buffett and Marks, holds that American Express's irreplicable closed-loop network — functioning simultaneously as issuer, processor, and merchant acquirer — constitutes a durable competitive moat that justifies acquisition at current valuations of approximately 19x earnings. The most significant dissent came from Mr. Greenblatt, who acknowledged the business's quality but argued that the absence of a meaningful valuation discount deprives the position of an adequate margin of safety; this view did not prevail because the majority concluded that a franchise of this caliber, with demonstrated pricing power and a premium cardholder base, warrants ownership at a fair price rather than waiting for a bargain that may never materialize. The Committee recommends initiating or adding to positions in AXP at current levels, with periodic reassessment of valuation and late-cycle credit conditions.

rows.name: Home Depot Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns Home Depot a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.65. The dominant argument, advanced by Mr. Buffett and endorsed by Mr. Marks, holds that Home Depot's 51% market share, $64 million in per-store revenue, entrenched Pro customer switching costs, and unmatched supply-chain scale constitute a durable competitive moat whose compounding economics justify the current valuation of approximately 20× forward earnings. The most significant dissent came from Mr. Greenblatt, who acknowledged the business's quality but argued that at 15.8× EV/EBITDA the market has already priced in that quality, leaving insufficient margin of safety for his return-on-capital framework. This objection did not prevail because the majority concluded that the moat's durability and continued share gains provide a margin of safety embedded in the business itself, not merely in the price. Ms. Wood's innovation-oriented objections were noted but found inapplicable to the company's category. The Committee recommends initiating a position at current levels.

rows.name: Honeywell International Inc.
rows.statement: The Committee assigns HON a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.636. The dominant argument, advanced by Messrs. Marks and Greenblatt and carrying the majority, holds that the post-aerospace spin-off has created a classic mispricing event: institutional indiscriminate selling of the restructured pure-play automation entity has compressed the valuation to approximately 6.6x EV/EBITDA, well below the franchise's normalized earnings power, while Honeywell's installed base across buildings, industrial processes, and defense sustains durable switching costs. The most significant dissent came from Mr. Buffett, who cautioned that the stark gap between the 7.8x trailing P/E and the 22x forward P/E signals genuine earnings deterioration post-separation rather than mere market confusion, and questioned whether the automation moat alone justifies a full position. This concern did not prevail because the majority judged the valuation distortion to be transition-year noise rather than structural impairment. The Committee recommends initiating a BUY position at current levels, with earnings normalization post-separation as the primary catalyst to monitor.

rows.name: Microsoft Corp.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee adopts a BUY position on Microsoft Corp. at a conviction score of 0.542. The dominant argument, advanced by Leopold Aschenbrenner and Cathie Wood, holds that Microsoft is the most deeply integrated enterprise AI platform in existence, that its $116 billion FY2026 capital expenditure represents an unprecedented infrastructure bet positioned at every critical intersection of AI monetization, and that conventional valuation frameworks understate the earnings trajectory of a regime-shift moment. The most significant dissent came from Warren Buffett, Howard Marks, and Joel Greenblatt, who argued that at 28.7 times earnings and a $3.9 trillion market capitalization, Microsoft's acknowledged greatness is already fully reflected in the price, leaving negligible margin of safety. This dissent did not prevail because the Committee judged that the structural depth of Microsoft's AI positioning — spanning Azure, Copilot, and enterprise software switching costs — presents asymmetric upside that modestly outweighs the valuation risk. The Committee recommends initiating a measured position with disciplined attention to capex returns and AI monetization milestones.

rows.name: NVIDIA Corp.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Furton Research Investment Committee assigns NVIDIA a final score of **0.519** and a position of **BUY**. The dominant argument carrying the majority held that NVIDIA is not a conventional cyclical hardware company but the critical infrastructure layer of an ongoing, multi-trillion-dollar AI buildout whose scaling trajectory has not yet been priced in — a thesis advanced most forcefully by Aschenbrenner and Wood, who emphasized CUDA ecosystem lock-in, sustained hyperscaler demand, and Wright's Law cost dynamics supporting durable revenue growth well beyond consensus estimates. The most significant dissent, articulated by Buffett, Marks, and Greenblatt, cautioned that extraordinary fundamentals are already substantially reflected in a $5+ trillion market capitalization, introducing concentration and valuation risk that limits the margin of safety. This dissent did not prevail because the committee judged that the empirical revenue trajectory and structural demand evidence outweighed traditional valuation concerns, though the narrow score reflects genuine uncertainty. The Committee recommends a **measured accumulation** of NVDA shares, with position sizing disciplined by the acknowledged valuation risk.

rows.name: Salesforce Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns Salesforce a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.5, reflecting a narrow and contested majority. The dominant argument, advanced by Cathie Wood and Howard Marks, holds that Salesforce's durable competitive moat—anchored in deep switching costs, 20.7% market share, and $14.4 billion in free cash flow—is being meaningfully reinforced by Agentforce, whose agentic AI platform positions the company to capture a genuine regime shift in enterprise software at a valuation that has corrected from peak levels. The most significant dissent, led by Warren Buffett and Joel Greenblatt, contended that at 27–31x earnings the stock prices in optimistic AI outcomes while leaving insufficient margin of safety, and that Agentforce may represent defensive moat maintenance rather than transformative expansion. This dissent did not prevail because the majority judged the asymmetry of Agentforce's platform economics and Salesforce's incumbent data advantages sufficient to justify a modest position at current prices. The Committee recommends a measured initial BUY with disciplined position sizing commensurate with the low conviction score.

rows.name: Goldman Sachs Group Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns Goldman Sachs a final score of 0.353 and a position of **BUY**. The dominant argument, advanced most forcefully by Howard Marks, held that a 12.8x forward P/E on a franchise generating 20.7% ROE represents a meaningful discount — the market is pricing Goldman as a commodity bank rather than an elite advisory and trading operation, and that cyclicality is already embedded in the multiple. The most significant dissent came from Warren Buffett and Joel Greenblatt, who argued that Goldman's earnings are inherently lumpy and cyclical, that 2.52x book value is not cheap for a balance-sheet-intensive financial institution, and that the magic-formula framework cannot reliably assess returns on $1.6 trillion in financial assets. Their objection did not prevail because the majority judged the valuation discount sufficiently compensates for cyclical risk given the strength of the franchise. The Committee recommends a modest, conviction-weighted accumulation at current levels, with position sizing reflecting the narrow margin of safety.

rows.name: Amgen Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Furton Research Investment Committee assigns Amgen Inc. a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.312, reflecting a modest but affirmative position. The dominant argument, advanced by Howard Marks and carrying the majority, held that Amgen's well-documented risks — biosimilar erosion, patent cliffs, and moderate top-line growth — are already substantially discounted in a forward earnings multiple of 14–18x, while $5 billion in annual free cash flow and a deep pipeline provide asymmetric upside if MariTide or Imdelltra deliver. The most significant dissent came from Warren Buffett, who argued that paying 25x trailing earnings for a business compounding at 6–7% offers insufficient margin of safety, particularly given the inherent unpredictability of pharmaceutical pipelines. This view did not prevail because the committee judged that forward valuation, rather than trailing multiples, more accurately captures the risk-reward balance at current prices. The Committee recommends initiating a measured position, sized to reflect the narrow margin of conviction and subject to reassessment upon Phase 3 pipeline readouts.

rows.name: Walt Disney Co.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee adopts a modest BUY position on DIS. The dominant argument, advanced by Howard Marks and carrying the majority, holds that Disney's unrivaled IP flywheel and parks moat are priced near the ten-year valuation median rather than at a premium, offering asymmetric upside should streaming profitability inflect further and the market re-rate the company beyond a "modestly growing conglomerate." The most significant dissent came from Warren Buffett and Joel Greenblatt, who argued that at approximately 23× earnings, Disney offers fair value at best—not the bargain price their frameworks demand—given capital consumption from the streaming transition, declining linear networks, and diluted returns on capital from legacy Fox goodwill. This dissent did not prevail because it conceded the quality of the franchise while failing to identify a catalyst for material downside, leaving the risk-reward modestly favorable rather than unattractive. The Committee recommends a measured accumulation at current levels with disciplined position sizing reflecting the narrow margin of safety.

rows.name: Merck & Co. Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee adopts a BUY position on Merck & Co. with moderate conviction. The dominant argument, advanced by Howard Marks and carrying the majority, holds that Keytruda's well-publicized 2028 patent cliff is already substantially discounted in the stock's 17x forward earnings multiple, and that the combination of Winrevair's cardiometabolic optionality, the subcutaneous QLEX formulation extending competitive positioning, and remaining Keytruda runway offers asymmetric upside at current prices — a second-level insight that the consensus view is too pessimistic. The most significant dissent, articulated by Warren Buffett and Joel Greenblatt, centered on the genuine uncertainty of post-cliff earnings power given Keytruda's approximately 40% revenue concentration, arguing that forecasting pharmaceutical profitability through a major patent expiry is inherently unreliable and that returns on capital may deteriorate materially. This dissent did not prevail because the valuation already embeds considerable skepticism, limiting downside. The Committee recommends initiating a measured position at current levels with disciplined review as 2028 visibility improves.

rows.name: Visa Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns Visa Inc. a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.304. The dominant argument, advanced most forcefully by Mr. Buffett and carrying the majority, holds that Visa operates as an unrivaled toll booth on global commerce — its self-reinforcing network of 4.5 billion cards and 130 million merchant locations, combined with negligible capital requirements and exceptional returns on equity, constitutes a durable franchise whose compounding power justifies a premium valuation. The most significant dissent, articulated by Messrs. Marks and Greenblatt, centered on valuation discipline: at approximately 30x trailing earnings and 17x price-to-book, the stock prices in considerable perfection during the later stages of an optimism cycle. This concern did not prevail because the Committee judged that Visa's capital-light economics and secular growth in digital payments — including the transformative China market opportunity — sufficiently underwrite sustained earnings growth to reward today's buyer. The Committee recommends initiating a position at current levels with disciplined sizing reflecting the elevated multiple.
